# HashSet equality policy reference

The checked-in corpus contains 7976 independent executions of Framework HashSet<int> (CLR 4.0.30319.42000).
Expected data is generated by the development-only C# program
[hashset-comparers.cs](../reference/hashset-comparers.cs), using the installed
Framework64 compiler and runtime. No original Pascal compiler is executed.
The native C++ test compiles [hashset-comparers-program.pas](hashset-comparers-program.pas)
with this project's compiler, then compares exact output and bilingual error codes.

Reproduce on Windows with ../reference/generate-hashset-comparers.ps1.
Normalized LF SHA-256 of hashset-comparers-reference.tsv:
5d3b49ccf9a7f2ba8e9a7673b7b1a451e5f9bcf1b0849121bb50a4a161f288ff.

Rows contain operation, initial storage shape, policy, other source kind, callback
mutation, hash/equality phase, callback ordinal, exact trace, and error code.
Policies include Default and several user comparers with negative constant hashes
and distinct equivalence classes. Shapes include never initialized, initialized
empty, cleared, collision-filled, sparse and removed-slot collections. Sources
include arrays with duplicates, same/different policy sets, self, nil, empty and
strict supersets. Tests cover constructors, retained Comparer identity, Copy,
PABCSystem set operators, every implemented set relation/algebra operation,
Contains/in, TryGetValue, RemoveWhere, TrimExcess, CopyTo and slot reuse.

Callbacks throw, grow, clear, compact, remove values, replace or nil the external
set variable. Fault observers use existing IEnumerator.Dispose behavior and
record retained aliases, final slots/counts/policies and an old enumerator.
General source try/finally remains pending. The corpus uses finite selected
reentrant cases; undefined/corrupted legacy callback loops are not a completeness
claim. A development reference run exposed an infinite legacy chain loop during
reentrant mutation; such cases are excluded, not treated as passing compatibility.

Source audit: PABCSystem.pas HashSet operators construct with Default, while
Copy(hs) explicitly passes hs.Comparer. Framework HashSet.cs constructors,
CopyFrom, InternalGetHashCode, AddIfNotPresent, Remove, Clear and set helpers
supply the storage and call-order contract:
https://github.com/microsoft/referencesource/blob/main/System.Core/System/Collections/Generic/HashSet.cs

No managed reference executable or C# source is installed in the portable package.
The corpus does not prove general Object virtual overrides, custom comparer
Object.Equals overrides, source generics, inheritance, boxing, variance,
StringComparer, Dictionary policies or comparer-aware LINQ/query overloads.
